questions: Is m_supportGeneration[] accessed from multiple threads? The code uses memory_order_acquire for m_connected but m_supportGeneration is a plain array, which could lead to data races if pollChannelSupport() and applyConnectedState() run on different threads.

Can d.request[0] be valid when d.length == 0? The code accesses d.request[0] unconditionally for the NRC string, but only iterates through d.request[0..d.length-1]. If the C library allows d.length == 0 with d.dropped > 0, this would read potentially uninitialized memory.

Is the timer callback pollChannelSupport() guaranteed to run only on the main thread? The coalesce timer is a QTimer, which typically fires in the thread where it was created, but this should be documented or verified.
nits: Consider making m_supportGeneration atomic<uint32_t>[ECUIO_SESSION_INFO_MAX_CHANNELS] or protecting it with a mutex to ensure thread safety regardless of call patterns.
Add a bounds check before accessing d.request[0] in channelSupportText(): if (d.length > 0) to handle the edge case where the C library might provide d.length == 0.
Consider adding a comment documenting that pollChannelSupport() and applyConnectedState() must both execute on the main thread, or use QThread::currentThread() assertions for validation.
The pid_bitmap iteration could be simplified by using bit manipulation instead of the complex index calculation: pid_bitmap[(pid-1)/8] & (0x80u >> ((pid-1)%8)) is correct but hard to read.
